sections.visa: Indian passport holders need a visa to enter Japan for tourism; apply through a VFS-authorized center with proof of itinerary, hotel bookings, and bank statements. Processing typically takes 5-7 working days. Many Western nationalities (US, UK, EU, Australia) can enter visa-free for stays under 90 days.
sections.best_time_to_visit: Best time to visit is late March to May (cherry blossom season) or October to November (autumn foliage). Summers (June-August) are hot and humid with a rainy season in June. Winters are cold and dry, especially in the north.
sections.local_customs: Bowing is a common greeting; a slight nod is fine for tourists. Remove shoes before entering homes, temples, and some restaurants. Tipping is not customary and can be considered rude. Speak quietly on public transport and avoid eating while walking. Queue in orderly lines for trains.
sections.packing_tips: Pack layers since temperature swings between day and night can be large. Comfortable walking shoes are essential due to extensive walking in cities. A compact umbrella is useful year-round due to sudden rain. In summer, bring breathable fabrics and a portable fan; in winter, pack a heavy coat, gloves, and thermal layers.
sections.safety_notes: Japan is considered very safe for travelers, with low violent crime rates. Natural disaster risk (earthquakes, typhoons) exists; familiarize yourself with basic earthquake safety. Pickpocketing is rare but stay alert in crowded tourist areas like Shibuya and Shinjuku.

sections.visa: Indian passport holders require a Schengen visa to enter France, applied for at least 15 days in advance via VFS Global, with proof of travel insurance, accommodation, and return tickets. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens and many other nationalities can enter visa-free for short stays.
sections.best_time_to_visit: Best time to visit is April to June or September to October for mild weather and fewer crowds. July and August are peak tourist season with warm weather but higher prices. Winters (Dec-Feb) are cold and grey but good for holiday markets and lower airfares.
sections.local_customs: Greet shopkeepers with 'Bonjour' before starting a conversation; skipping this is seen as rude. Tipping (5-10%) is appreciated but not mandatory since service is usually included. Dress reasonably smart, especially for restaurants and churches. Meals are leisurely; rushing through dinner is unusual.
sections.packing_tips: Pack a versatile jacket or trench coat for unpredictable weather. Comfortable but stylish walking shoes are recommended, since cobblestone streets are common. In summer, light layers and a scarf for cooler evenings; in winter, a warm coat, gloves, and waterproof boots.
sections.safety_notes: Paris is generally safe but has a notable pickpocketing problem near tourist sites (Eiffel Tower, Metro, Montmartre). Avoid displaying valuables openly. Occasional protests/strikes can disrupt public transport; check local news before travel.

sections.visa: Indian passport holders can obtain a visa-on-arrival for stays up to 30 days at major entry points, or apply for an e-visa in advance. A valid return ticket and proof of accommodation are usually required. Visa exemption schemes have changed periodically, so checking current rules close to travel dates is recommended.
sections.best_time_to_visit: Best time to visit is November to February (cool, dry season). March to May is very hot. June to October is the rainy/monsoon season with frequent afternoon downpours but lush scenery and fewer tourists.
sections.local_customs: The 'wai' (a slight bow with palms together) is a traditional greeting; tourists aren't obligated to use it but it's appreciated. Dress modestly when visiting temples (covered shoulders and knees). Never touch anyone's head or point your feet at people or Buddha images. Public displays of anger are frowned upon.
sections.packing_tips: Pack lightweight, breathable clothing due to heat and humidity. Bring a modest cover-up (scarf or sarong) for temple visits. During monsoon season (Jun-Oct), pack a compact rain poncho or umbrella and quick-dry clothing. Sunscreen and insect repellent are essential year-round.
sections.safety_notes: Bangkok is generally safe for tourists but watch for common scams (gem scams, overpriced tuk-tuk tours). Street food is generally safe if from busy stalls with high turnover. During monsoon season, flash flooding can disrupt low-lying areas.

sections.visa: Indian passport holders require a Schengen visa to enter Iceland, similar to other Schengen countries, applied for through VFS Global with proof of accommodation, insurance, and sufficient funds. EU/EEA and several other nationalities can enter visa-free.
sections.best_time_to_visit: Best time to visit for the Northern Lights is September to March (long dark nights). Best time for hiking, midnight sun, and accessible highland roads is June to August. Weather is highly changeable year-round regardless of season.
sections.local_customs: Icelanders are informal; first names are used even in professional settings. Tipping is not customary and not expected in restaurants or taxis. Punctuality is valued. Removing shoes when entering homes is common practice.
sections.packing_tips: Pack windproof and waterproof outer layers regardless of season, as weather changes rapidly. Layered clothing (base, insulating, and shell layers) is essential. In winter, bring thermal wear, waterproof boots with good grip for ice, and a heavy coat. In summer, still pack a warm layer and rain jacket for cool, wet spells.
sections.safety_notes: Iceland is one of the safest countries in the world with very low crime rates. The main risks are weather and terrain related: sudden storms, icy roads, and dangerous coastal areas (e.g. sneaker waves at black sand beaches). Always check road and weather conditions before driving.
